records.source: לַמְנַצֵּ֤חַ׀לְעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּ֨ר׀לַיהוָ֗ה אֶת־דִּ֭בְרֵי הַשִּׁירָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את בְּי֤וֹם הִֽצִּיל־יְהוָ֘ה אוֹת֥וֹ מִכַּ֥ף כָּל־אֹ֝יְבָ֗יו וּמִיַּ֥ד שָׁאֽוּל׃
records.gloss: For the director. Of [the] servant of YHWH, of David, who spoke to YHWH the words of this song on [the] day YHWH delivered him from [the] palm of all his enemies and from [the] hand of Saul.
pieces: For the music director. By David, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He sang the words of this song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rescued him from the power of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

L.1: For the director: of the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, of David, who spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the words of this song on the day [when] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delivered him from the palm of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

R.1: For the leader of the music. By David, who served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He sang this song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved him from all his enemies, and from Saul.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the same song as 2 Samuel 22
decisions.reason: With small differences, this psalm is the song David sings in 2 Samuel 22, which has a shorter title of the same kind. Its setting is the end of David's wars, when Saul was dead and the LORD had given him rest from his enemies.

decisions.choice: the servant of the LORD: a title of honor
decisions.reason: "Servant of the LORD" is the title of Moses (Deuteronomy 34:5) and Joshua (Joshua 24:29). It is given to David here and in the title of Psalm 36.

decisions.choice: the palm of all his enemies: their power
decisions.reason: The palm and the hand stand for power and control.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

records.heading: David's song of rescue and victory

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֡ר אֶרְחָמְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה חִזְקִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said, I love you, YHWH, my strength.
pieces: He said: "I love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my strength.

L.2: And he said: "I love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my strength.

R.2: He said: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You make me strong.

decisions.choice: I love you: a love deep within
decisions.reason: The verb (racham) is used of the tender love of a parent for a child (103:13); only here is it used of a person's love for God. The line is not in 2 Samuel 22.

decisions.choice: the song as one speech
decisions.reason: The whole song, to verse 51, is David's speech; the quotation opens here and closes at the end of the psalm.

decisions.choice: You make me strong
decisions.reason: Readable turns the title into a sentence.

records.source: יְהוָ֤ה׀סַֽלְעִ֥י וּמְצוּדָתִ֗י וּמְפַ֫לְטִ֥י אֵלִ֣י צ֭וּרִי אֶֽחֱסֶה־בּ֑וֹ מָֽגִנִּ֥י וְקֶֽרֶן־יִ֝שְׁעִ֗י מִשְׂגַּבִּֽי׃
records.gloss: YHWH [is] my rock and my stronghold and my deliverer, my God, my rock, I take refuge in him, my shield and [the] horn of my salvation, my high refuge.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is my cliff, my stronghold, the one who sets me free; my God is my rock, and I shelter in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is my shield, my strong salvation, my tower on the heights.

L.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] my crag and my stronghold and my deliverer, my God, my rock in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my high refuge.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is like a high rock where I am safe. He is like a fort, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescues me. My God is like a rock where I can run for safety. He protects me like a shield. He is strong to save me. He is like a tower high above my enemies.

decisions.choice: rock, stronghold, high refuge: places of safety in the hills
decisions.reason: David hid from Saul in the rocky heights and strongholds of the wilderness (1 Samuel 23:14, 25). The words for these places (sela', metsudah, misgav) become names for God himself.

decisions.choice: the horn of my salvation: my strong savior
decisions.reason: A horn is the strength of an animal and so a picture of power (75:11; 1 Samuel 2:1); "the horn of my salvation" is the power that saves me.

decisions.choice: I take refuge in him
decisions.reason: As in 7:2.

decisions.choice: my strong salvation (B); He is strong to save me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the horn means (m2).

decisions.choice: like a high rock, like a fort, like a tower
decisions.reason: Readable makes the pictures comparisons, so that young readers do not take them literally.

records.source: מְ֭הֻלָּל אֶקְרָ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּמִן־אֹ֝יְבַ֗י אִוָּשֵֽׁעַ׃
records.gloss: [The one who is] to be praised I call [on], YHWH, and from my enemies I am saved.
pieces: I call on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who is worthy of praise, and from my enemies I am rescued.

L.4: [The one who is] worthy of praise I call [on], {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and from my enemies I am saved.

R.4: I call to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who deserves all praise, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves me from my enemies.

decisions.choice: I call, I am saved: what always happens
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the unfinished form: whenever David calls, he is saved. Verses 5-20 then tell one great rescue.

decisions.choice: the one to be praised: worthy of praise
decisions.reason: The word (mehullal) means praised, deserving praise (48:2; 96:4).

records.source: אֲפָפ֥וּנִי חֶבְלֵי־מָ֑וֶת וְֽנַחֲלֵ֖י בְלִיַּ֣עַל יְבַֽעֲתֽוּנִי׃
records.gloss: They encompassed me, [the] cords of death, and torrents of worthlessness terrified me.
pieces: Death's ropes were wrapped around me; floods of ruin overwhelmed me with terror.

L.5: The cords of death encompassed me, and torrents of destruction terrified me.

R.5: Death was like ropes tied around me. Danger poured over me like a flood, and I was terrified.

decisions.choice: cords: ropes, or birth pangs
decisions.reason: The word (chevel) means a rope or a pain of childbirth; with "snares" in verse 6 it means ropes. 2 Samuel 22:5 has "the breakers of death".

decisions.choice: worthlessness: ruin, destruction
decisions.reason: The word (beliyya'al) means what is worthless and destructive; it later became a name for evil and for Satan (2 Corinthians 6:15).

decisions.choice: torrents: death pictured as a flood
decisions.reason: The waters of death rise and sweep the singer away, as in 69:2-3; God draws him out in verse 17.

records.source: חֶבְלֵ֣י שְׁא֣וֹל סְבָב֑וּנִי קִ֝דְּמ֗וּנִי מ֣וֹקְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: [The] cords of Sheol surrounded me; [the] snares of death confronted me.
pieces: The ropes of Sheol coiled around me; death's traps lay right in front of me.

L.6: The cords of Sheol surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me.

R.6: It was as if the place of the dead had me tied up. Death had set traps for me, and I could not get away.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: As in 6:6.

decisions.choice: the snares of death confronted me: death stood in my way
decisions.reason: Death is a hunter whose traps meet the singer at every turn (116:3).

records.source: בַּצַּר־לִ֤י׀אֶֽקְרָ֣א יְהוָה֮ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהַ֪י אֲשַׁ֫וֵּ֥עַ יִשְׁמַ֣ע מֵהֵיכָל֣וֹ קוֹלִ֑י וְ֝שַׁוְעָתִ֗י לְפָנָ֤יו׀תָּב֬וֹא בְאָזְנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: In my distress I called [on] YHWH, and to my God I cried for help; he heard from his temple my voice, and my cry before him came into his ears.
pieces: When I was hard pressed I called on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and cried out to my God. Out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listened to my voice; my cry came before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and reached {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears.

L.7: In my distress I called [on] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to my God I cried for help; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard my voice from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, and my cry before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} came into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears.

R.7: When I was in trouble, I called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I begged my God to help me. He was in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard me. My cry reached {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears.

decisions.choice: his temple: God's dwelling in heaven
decisions.reason: As in 11:4, the temple is God's palace in heaven, from which he comes down in verses 8-16.

decisions.choice: I called, he heard: the story of the rescue
decisions.reason: Here the song turns to tell the rescue as a past event.

records.source: וַתִּגְעַ֬שׁ וַתִּרְעַ֨שׁ׀הָאָ֗רֶץ וּמוֹסְדֵ֣י הָרִ֣ים יִרְגָּ֑זוּ וַ֝יִּתְגָּֽעֲשׁ֗וּ כִּי־חָ֥רָה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And shook and quaked the earth, and [the] foundations of [the] mountains trembled and shook, for it burned to him.
pieces: Then the earth shuddered and rocked; the roots of the mountains trembled and were shaken, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was furious.

L.8: And the earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the mountains trembled and shook, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry.

R.8: Then the earth shook. Even the mountains shook to their roots, because God was very angry.

decisions.choice: the earth shook: the LORD comes as at Sinai
decisions.reason: Verses 8-16 picture the LORD coming down in storm and earthquake, as he did at Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:16-18) and when he led Israel out of Egypt (Judges 5:4-5; 68:8-9).

decisions.choice: it burned to him: he was angry
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it burned to him", a common way of saying that anger flared up (Genesis 4:5).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names who was angry.

records.source: עָ֘לָ֤ה עָשָׁ֨ן׀בְּאַפּ֗וֹ וְאֵשׁ־מִפִּ֥יו תֹּאכֵ֑ל גֶּ֝חָלִ֗ים בָּעֲר֥וּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Smoke went up in his nose, and fire from his mouth devoured; coals burned from it.
pieces: Smoke rose from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nostrils, and fire that consumes came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth; burning coals flamed out of it.

L.9: Smoke went up from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nostrils, and fire from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth devoured; coals blazed from it.

R.9: Smoke came out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nose. Fire that burns up everything came out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, with red-hot coals.

decisions.choice: smoke in his nose: a picture of anger
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the nose is the seat of anger (the word 'af means both); the snorting of fury is pictured as smoke and fire.

decisions.choice: fire from his mouth: God's holy anger
decisions.reason: The LORD is a consuming fire (Deuteronomy 4:24). The picture is poetry for God's power against those who oppose him.

records.source: וַיֵּ֣ט שָׁ֭מַיִם וַיֵּרַ֑ד וַ֝עֲרָפֶ֗ל תַּ֣חַת רַגְלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he bent [the] heavens and came down, and thick darkness [was] under his feet.
pieces: He bowed the heavens low and came down; storm clouds were dark beneath {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

L.10: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bent the heavens and came down, and thick darkness [was] under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

R.10: He opened the sky and came down. Dark clouds were under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

decisions.choice: bent the heavens: bowed the sky down
decisions.reason: The verb (natah) means to stretch out or bend; the sky bows down as God comes (144:5).

decisions.choice: thick darkness: the dark cloud around God
decisions.reason: The thick darkness ('arafel) is the cloud in which God came to Sinai (Exodus 20:21; Deuteronomy 4:11).

records.source: וַיִּרְכַּ֣ב עַל־כְּ֭רוּב וַיָּעֹ֑ף וַ֝יֵּ֗דֶא עַל־כַּנְפֵי־רֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: And he rode on a cherub and flew, and swooped on [the] wings of [the] wind.
pieces: Riding on a cherub, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} flew; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swooped down on the wings of the wind.

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rode on a cherub and flew, and swooped on the wings of the wind.

R.11: He flew, riding on a cherub. He came down fast, carried by the wind.

decisions.choice: a cherub: a winged being who serves God
decisions.reason: Cherubim guard God's presence (Genesis 3:24) and carry his throne (Ezekiel 10); the LORD is "enthroned on the cherubim" (80:2; 1 Samuel 4:4). Here a cherub is his chariot.

decisions.choice: swooped: flew swiftly down
decisions.reason: The verb (da'ah) is used of a bird of prey swooping (Deuteronomy 28:49); 2 Samuel 22:11 has a similar-looking word meaning "was seen".

records.source: יָ֤שֶׁת חֹ֨שֶׁךְ׀סִתְר֗וֹ סְבִֽיבוֹתָ֥יו סֻכָּת֑וֹ חֶשְׁכַת־מַ֝֗יִם עָבֵ֥י שְׁחָקִֽים׃
records.gloss: He made darkness his hiding place around him, his canopy darkness of waters, clouds of skies.
pieces: He wrapped {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} in darkness and hid in it; all around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was a tent of dark rain clouds, thick clouds of the sky.

L.12: He made darkness {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hiding place, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} canopy around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, dark waters, clouds of the skies.

R.12: He hid {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} in darkness. He was covered with dark rain clouds like a tent.

decisions.choice: his canopy: his tent or booth
decisions.reason: The word (sukkah) is a shelter or booth; the storm clouds are God's tent (Job 36:29).

decisions.choice: darkness of waters: dark rain clouds
decisions.reason: Clouds heavy with water are dark; the storm hides God from sight (97:2).

records.source: מִנֹּ֗גַהּ נֶ֫גְדּ֥וֹ עָבָ֥יו עָבְר֑וּ בָּ֝רָ֗ד וְגַֽחֲלֵי־אֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: From [the] brightness before him his clouds passed, hail and coals of fire.
pieces: Out of the brightness in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clouds broke through, with hail and burning coals.

L.13: From the brightness before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clouds passed through, hail and coals of fire.

R.13: From the bright light around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, hail and burning coals burst out of the clouds.

decisions.choice: brightness: the light around God
decisions.reason: The brightness (nogah) is the blazing light of God's presence (Ezekiel 1:4, 28).

decisions.choice: hail and coals of fire: hail and lightning
decisions.reason: As in the plague on Egypt, hail falls with fire (Exodus 9:23-24); the "coals of fire" are lightning.

records.source: וַיַּרְעֵ֬ם בַּשָּׁמַ֨יִם׀יְֽהוָ֗ה וְ֭עֶלְיוֹן יִתֵּ֣ן קֹל֑וֹ בָּ֝רָ֗ד וְגַֽחֲלֵי־אֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And thundered in the heavens YHWH, and [the] Most High gave his voice, hail and coals of fire.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} thundered in the heavens; the Most High raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, with hail and burning coals.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thundered in the heavens, and the Most High gave forth {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, hail and coals of fire.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} thundered from the sky. The God who is above all spoke with a voice like thunder. Hail and burning coals came down.

decisions.choice: gave his voice: thundered
decisions.reason: God's voice is the thunder (29:3-9).

decisions.choice: the Most High: God above all
decisions.reason: The title ('Elyon) is explained at 7:18 and 9:3.

decisions.choice: hail and coals of fire: repeated from verse 13
decisions.reason: The last words repeat verse 13. They are not in 2 Samuel 22:14 or in the ancient Greek translation of this psalm, and may have been copied by mistake from the line above. They are in the Hebrew text and are kept.

decisions.choice: The God who is above all
decisions.reason: As in 7:18.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח חִ֭צָּיו וַיְפִיצֵ֑ם וּבְרָקִ֥ים רָ֝ב וַיְהֻמֵּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he sent his arrows and scattered them, and lightnings he shot and routed them.
pieces: He let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arrows fly and scattered the enemy; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hurled lightning bolts and threw them into confusion.

L.15: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arrows and scattered them, and shot lightnings and routed them.

R.15: He shot {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arrows and made the enemy run away. He threw lightning at them and they did not know where to go.

decisions.choice: his arrows: lightning
decisions.reason: The lightning bolts are God's arrows (77:18; Habakkuk 3:11).

decisions.choice: routed them: threw them into panic
decisions.reason: The verb (hamam) is used of God throwing an army into confusion (Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10).

decisions.choice: the enemy
decisions.reason: "Them" are David's enemies; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וַיֵּ֤רָא֨וּ׀אֲפִ֥יקֵי מַ֗יִם וַֽיִּגָּלוּ֮ מוֹסְד֪וֹת תֵּ֫בֵ֥ל מִגַּעֲרָ֣תְךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה מִ֝נִּשְׁמַ֗ת ר֣וּחַ אַפֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And were seen [the] channels of water, and were uncovered [the] foundations of [the] world, at your rebuke, YHWH, at [the] blast of [the] breath of your nose.
pieces: The beds of the sea came into view, and the world's foundations lay bare at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rebuke, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, at the blast of breath from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nostrils.

L.16: And the channels of the waters appeared, and the foundations of the world were laid bare at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rebuke, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, at the blast of the breath of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nostrils.

R.16: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} shouted in anger and breathed out hard, the water was pushed back. The bottom of the sea and the deep roots of the earth could be seen.

decisions.choice: the blast of your nostrils: as at the Red Sea
decisions.reason: At the sea "by the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up" (Exodus 15:8), and the seabed was laid bare. The rescue of David is told like the rescue at the sea.

decisions.choice: rebuke: a stern command
decisions.reason: God's rebuke (ge'arah) drives back the waters (104:7).

decisions.choice: your rebuke: the song speaks to God
decisions.reason: The song turns for a moment from "he" to "you"; 2 Samuel 22:16 keeps "his".

records.source: יִשְׁלַ֣ח מִ֭מָּרוֹם יִקָּחֵ֑נִי יַֽ֝מְשֵׁ֗נִי מִמַּ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: He sent from on high, he took me, he drew me out of many waters.
pieces: From on high {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and seized me; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pulled me out of deep waters.

L.17: He reached down from on high, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took me; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drew me out of many waters.

R.17: He reached down from heaven and grabbed me. He pulled me out of the deep water.

decisions.choice: drew me out: the verb of Moses' name
decisions.reason: The verb (mashah) is found only here, in 2 Samuel 22:17 and in Exodus 2:10, where Pharaoh's daughter names Moses because she "drew him out" of the water.

decisions.choice: many waters: the floods of death and danger
decisions.reason: The waters of verse 5; many waters are the forces of chaos and death (32:6; 144:7).

decisions.choice: he sent: he reached out his hand
decisions.reason: "He sent" is short for "he sent out his hand" (144:7).

records.source: יַצִּילֵ֗נִי מֵאֹיְבִ֥י עָ֑ז וּ֝מִשֹּׂנְאַ֗י כִּֽי־אָמְצ֥וּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: He rescued me from my enemy, strong, and from those who hated me, for they were stronger than I.
pieces: He snatched me away from my powerful enemy, from those who hated me, because they were stronger than I was.

L.18: He rescued me from my strong enemy and from those who hated me, for they were too strong for me.

R.18: He saved me from my powerful enemy and from all who hated me. They were too strong for me to fight.

decisions.choice: my strong enemy: one enemy above all
decisions.reason: The singular "enemy" may be Saul (verse 1) or every enemy taken together.

decisions.choice: they were too strong for me: rescue by God alone
decisions.reason: David does not boast of his own strength; the rescue is God's work.

records.source: יְקַדְּמ֥וּנִי בְיוֹם־אֵידִ֑י וַֽיְהִי־יְהוָ֖ה לְמִשְׁעָ֣ן לִֽי׃
records.gloss: They confronted me in [the] day of my calamity, but YHWH became a support to me.
pieces: They came at me on my day of disaster, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} held me up.

L.19: They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became a support to me.

R.19: They attacked me when I was in deep trouble. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took care of me.

decisions.choice: calamity: ruin, disaster
decisions.reason: The word ('ed) is a crushing disaster (Proverbs 1:26-27).

decisions.choice: support: a staff to lean on
decisions.reason: The word (mish'an) is something to lean on, like a staff (23:4 uses a related word).

records.source: וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֥נִי לַמֶּרְחָ֑ב יְ֝חַלְּצֵ֗נִי כִּ֘י חָ֥פֵֽץ בִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And he brought me out to the broad place; he rescued me, for he delighted in me.
pieces: He led me out into open country; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set me free, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was pleased with me.

L.20: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me out into the broad place; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued me, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delighted in me.

R.20: He brought me out to a safe, open place. He saved me because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was happy with me.

decisions.choice: the broad place: freedom and safety
decisions.reason: Trouble in Hebrew is a narrow place where one is hemmed in; rescue is room to move (4:2; 118:5).

decisions.choice: he delighted in me: he was pleased with me
decisions.reason: The verb (chafets) is used of God's pleasure in a person (22:9; 2 Samuel 15:26).

records.source: יִגְמְלֵ֣נִי יְהוָ֣ה כְּצִדְקִ֑י כְּבֹ֥ר יָ֝דַ֗י יָשִׁ֥יב לִֽי׃
records.gloss: YHWH dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to [the] cleanness of my hands he repaid me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} treated me as my right conduct deserved; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rewarded me because my hands were clean.

L.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repaid me.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was good to me because I did what was right. I had not done wrong, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed me.

decisions.choice: according to my righteousness: loyalty, not sinlessness
decisions.reason: David is not claiming that he never sinned. In the setting of the title he means that he stayed loyal to the LORD and did not take matters into his own hands; he twice spared Saul's life (1 Samuel 24 and 26). The same words close this section in verse 25.

decisions.choice: cleanness of my hands: innocence in what I have done
decisions.reason: Clean hands are hands that have done no wrong (24:4).

decisions.choice: dealt with me: repaid me
decisions.reason: As in 13:6.

records.source: כִּֽי־שָׁ֭מַרְתִּי דַּרְכֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־רָ֝שַׁ֗עְתִּי מֵאֱלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: For I have kept [the] ways of YHWH and have not acted wickedly from my God.
pieces: For I have walked in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s ways and have not turned from my God to do evil.

L.22: For I have kept the ways of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I have not acted wickedly [to depart] from my God.

R.22: I have obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I have not turned away from my God to do evil.

decisions.choice: acted wickedly from my God: left God to do wrong
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "act wickedly" and "from": to sin by leaving God.

decisions.choice: kept the ways of the LORD: lived as he commands
decisions.reason: The LORD's ways are the life he has commanded (Deuteronomy 8:6).

records.source: כִּ֣י כָל־מִשְׁפָּטָ֣יו לְנֶגְדִּ֑י וְ֝חֻקֹּתָ֗יו לֹא־אָסִ֥יר מֶֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: For all his judgments [are] before me, and his statutes I have not turned aside from me.
pieces: All {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings have been in front of me; I have not pushed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws aside.

L.23: For all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments [are] before me, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes I have not turned aside from me.

R.23: I keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws in mind. I have not stopped obeying {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rules.

decisions.choice: judgments, statutes: God's commands
decisions.reason: Two common words for God's law (Deuteronomy 4:1, 8).

decisions.choice: before me: always in view
decisions.reason: To keep the law before one's eyes is to live by it (16:8).

records.source: וָאֱהִ֣י תָמִ֣ים עִמּ֑וֹ וָ֝אֶשְׁתַּמֵּ֗ר מֵעֲוֺנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I was blameless with him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.
pieces: I was whole-hearted with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; I guarded myself from sin.

L.24: And I was blameless with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and I kept myself from my iniquity.

R.24: I was loyal to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all my heart. I kept myself from doing wrong.

decisions.choice: blameless: whole, with integrity
decisions.reason: As in 15:2.

decisions.choice: from my iniquity: from sinning
decisions.reason: "My iniquity" is the sin he might have committed; he kept himself from it.

records.source: וַיָּֽשֶׁב־יְהוָ֣ה לִ֣י כְצִדְקִ֑י כְּבֹ֥ר יָ֝דַ֗י לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And YHWH repaid me according to my righteousness, according to [the] cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rewarded me for doing right, for the clean hands {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could see.

L.25: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes.

R.25: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rewarded me because I did what was right. He saw that I had not done wrong.

decisions.choice: repaid me according to my righteousness: verse 21 again
decisions.reason: The words of verse 21 return, closing this part of the song.

decisions.choice: before his eyes: as God sees it
decisions.reason: The cleanness is what God himself sees, not only what others see.

records.source: עִם־חָסִ֥יד תִּתְחַסָּ֑ד עִם־גְּבַ֥ר תָּ֝מִ֗ים תִּתַּמָּֽם׃
records.gloss: With [the] loyal you show yourself loyal; with [the] blameless man you show yourself blameless.
pieces: To the faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful; to those of integrity {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show integrity.

L.26: With the loyal {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} loyal; with the blameless {{gender:person|man}} {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} blameless.

R.26: You keep faith with people who keep faith with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You are good to people who live good lives.

decisions.choice: you show yourself loyal: God answers people as they are
decisions.reason: Verses 26-27 state the rule behind verses 21-25: God deals with each person in keeping with how that person lives toward him.

decisions.choice: the loyal: one who keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word (chasid) is the one of 4:4 and 16:10.

decisions.choice: person, with "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word (gever) means a man, but here anyone who lives this way.

records.source: עִם־נָבָ֥ר תִּתְבָּרָ֑ר וְעִם־עִ֝קֵּ֗שׁ תִּתְפַּתָּֽל׃
records.gloss: With [the one who] purifies himself you show yourself pure, but with [the] crooked you show yourself twisted.
pieces: To the pure {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} prove {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} pure, but with the crooked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are subtle.

L.27: With the pure {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} pure, but with the crooked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} shrewd.

R.27: You are pure with people who are pure. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are clever with people who are twisted and false.

decisions.choice: with the crooked you are shrewd: God outwits them
decisions.reason: The verb (patal, to twist) is a different word from "crooked" ('iqqesh). God does not become crooked; he matches the schemes of the crooked and turns them back on them (Proverbs 3:34).

decisions.choice: the pure: one who keeps himself clean
decisions.reason: The form means one who purifies himself, keeping his life clean.

records.source: כִּֽי־אַ֭תָּה עַם־עָנִ֣י תוֹשִׁ֑יעַ וְעֵינַ֖יִם רָמ֣וֹת תַּשְׁפִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: For you save an afflicted people, but haughty eyes you bring low.
pieces: You rescue people who are humbled, but proud eyes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring down.

L.28: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save an afflicted people, but haughty eyes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring low.

R.28: You save people who are poor and humble. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring down people who are proud.

decisions.choice: afflicted: poor, humbled
decisions.reason: The word ('ani) means poor and pressed down, and so dependent on God (9:13).

decisions.choice: haughty eyes: pride
decisions.reason: Eyes raised high look down on others (101:5; Proverbs 6:17).

records.source: כִּֽי־אַ֭תָּה תָּאִ֣יר נֵרִ֑י יְהוָ֥ה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י יַגִּ֥יהַּ חָשְׁכִּֽי׃
records.gloss: For you light my lamp; YHWH my God makes bright my darkness.
pieces: You make my lamp shine; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God brightens my darkness.

L.29: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} light my lamp; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God makes my darkness bright.

R.29: You give me light like a lamp. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God makes my dark times bright.

decisions.choice: my lamp: my life and its future
decisions.reason: A burning lamp is a picture of life and hope; the lamp of the wicked goes out (Job 18:6). God keeps David's lamp burning.

decisions.choice: you ... the LORD: the song moves between "you" and "he"
decisions.reason: The line speaks to God and then of him, as songs of praise often do.

records.source: כִּֽי־בְ֭ךָ אָרֻ֣ץ גְּד֑וּד וּ֝בֵֽאלֹהַ֗י אֲדַלֶּג־שֽׁוּר׃
records.gloss: For by you I run [against] a troop, and by my God I leap over a wall.
pieces: With {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I can rush an armed band; by the strength of my God I can vault a wall.

L.30: For by {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I run [against] a troop, and by my God I leap over a wall.

R.30: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help I can attack a whole army. With God's help I can jump over a city wall.

decisions.choice: a troop: a raiding band
decisions.reason: The word (gedud) is a band of raiders (1 Samuel 30:8). The verb may mean "run" or, read slightly differently, "crush".

decisions.choice: leap over a wall: storm a city
decisions.reason: A wall is a city wall; with God's help David takes walled cities (2 Samuel 5:6-7).

decisions.choice: your help
decisions.reason: Readable says that "by you" means by God's help.

records.source: הָאֵל֮ תָּמִ֪ים דַּ֫רְכּ֥וֹ אִמְרַֽת־יְהוָ֥ה צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לְכֹ֤ל׀הַחֹסִ֬ים בּֽוֹ׃

L.31: [As for] God, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way [is] blameless; the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] refined; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] a shield to all who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.31: God always does what is right. What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is always true. He protects everyone who runs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety.

decisions.choice: refined: tested and proved pure
decisions.reason: As silver is refined (12:7), God's word has been tested and found true (Proverbs 30:5).

decisions.choice: blameless: whole, without flaw
decisions.reason: The word used of David in verse 24 is used of God's way.

decisions.choice: The God: this God
decisions.reason: With the article the word points to the God the song has been describing.

records.source: כִּ֤י מִ֣י אֱ֭לוֹהַּ מִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וּמִ֥י צ֝֗וּר זוּלָתִ֥י אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: For who [is] God except YHWH? And who [is] a rock except our God?

L.32: For who [is] God except {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? And who [is] a rock except our God?

R.32: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the only God. Only our God is strong and safe like a rock.

decisions.choice: who is God except the LORD?: there is none
decisions.reason: The questions expect the answer "no one" (Isaiah 44:8).

decisions.choice: God: Eloah
decisions.reason: The word here is 'Eloah, a poetic form of the word for God.

decisions.choice: statements
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into what they mean (m1).

records.source: הָ֭אֵל הַמְאַזְּרֵ֣נִי חָ֑יִל וַיִּתֵּ֖ן תָּמִ֣ים דַּרְכִּֽי׃
records.gloss: The God who girds me [with] strength and has made blameless my way,
pieces: the God who straps strength around me like a belt and makes my way secure,

L.33: The God who girds me [with] strength and has made my way blameless,

R.33: God makes me strong. He keeps me safe wherever I go.

decisions.choice: girds me with strength: gives me strength
decisions.reason: A soldier tied his belt tight before battle; God fastens strength on David like a belt (verse 40; 1 Samuel 2:4).

decisions.choice: made my way blameless: kept my path safe and whole
decisions.reason: The word (tamim) here means whole or unbroken: a road with no stumbling.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The description of God continues through verse 35, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: מְשַׁוֶּ֣ה רַ֭גְלַי כָּאַיָּל֑וֹת וְעַ֥ל בָּ֝מֹתַ֗י יַעֲמִידֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: making my feet like the does, and on my heights he makes me stand,
pieces: who makes my feet as sure as a deer's and sets me firm on the heights,

L.34: making my feet like the does', and on my heights {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes me stand,

R.34: He makes me sure-footed like a deer. He lets me stand safely high up in the mountains.

decisions.choice: like the does: sure-footed on the rocks
decisions.reason: Deer move swiftly and safely on steep crags (Habakkuk 3:19).

decisions.choice: my heights: the high ground
decisions.reason: To stand on the heights is to hold the high ground, safe and in command (Deuteronomy 32:13).

records.source: מְלַמֵּ֣ד יָ֭דַי לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְֽנִחֲתָ֥ה קֶֽשֶׁת־נְ֝חוּשָׁ֗ה זְרוֹעֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: training my hands for the battle, and bends a bow of bronze my arms.

R.35: He trains me to fight in battle. He makes my arms strong enough to bend a bow made of bronze.

decisions.choice: a bow of bronze: a bow only the strongest can bend
decisions.reason: Bows were made of wood and horn; a bow of bronze, or one fitted with bronze, would need great strength to draw (Job 20:24).

decisions.choice: the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: The description of God that began in verse 33 ends here.

records.source: וַתִּתֶּן־לִי֮ מָגֵ֪ן יִ֫שְׁעֶ֥ךָ וִֽימִינְךָ֥ תִסְעָדֵ֑נִי וְֽעַנְוַתְךָ֥ תַרְבֵּֽנִי׃

decisions.choice: your right hand supports me: not in 2 Samuel 22
decisions.reason: This line is not in 2 Samuel 22:36.

records.source: תַּרְחִ֣יב צַעֲדִ֣י תַחְתָּ֑י וְלֹ֥א מָ֝עֲד֗וּ קַרְסֻלָּֽי׃
records.gloss: You make wide my steps under me, and not have slipped my ankles.

decisions.reason: As in verse 20, room is safety; a wide path has no traps.

decisions.choice: ankles: what gives way in a fall
decisions.reason: The word (qarsol) is found only here and in 2 Samuel 22:37.

records.source: אֶרְדּ֣וֹף א֭וֹיְבַי וְאַשִּׂיגֵ֑ם וְלֹֽא־אָ֝שׁוּבעַד־כַּלּוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: I pursued my enemies and overtook them, and not did I turn back until they were finished.

R.38: I chased my enemies and caught them. I did not stop until they were all gone.

decisions.choice: I pursued my enemies: victory as God's gift
decisions.reason: David's victories are told as the work of the God who trains and arms him (verses 33-36, 40). In 2 Samuel 22:38 the verbs are "I pursued and destroyed".

records.source: אֶ֭מְחָצֵם וְלֹא־יֻ֣כְלוּ ק֑וּם יִ֝פְּל֗וּ תַּ֣חַת רַגְלָֽי׃
records.gloss: I smashed them, and not were they able to rise; they fell under my feet.

R.39: I beat them so badly that they could not get up. They fell down at my feet.

decisions.choice: under my feet: complete defeat
decisions.reason: A conquered enemy lay under the victor's feet (110:1; Joshua 10:24).

records.source: וַתְּאַזְּרֵ֣נִי חַ֭יִל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה תַּכְרִ֖יעַ קָמַ֣י תַּחְתָּֽי׃

L.40: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} girded me [with] strength for battle; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made those who rose against me bow down under me.

R.40: You made me strong for battle. You made my enemies fall down in front of me.

decisions.choice: girded me with strength
decisions.reason: As in verse 33.

decisions.choice: made bow down: brought to their knees
decisions.reason: The verb (kara') means to kneel or sink down, here in defeat.

records.source: וְֽאֹיְבַ֗י נָתַ֣תָּה לִּ֣י עֹ֑רֶף וּ֝מְשַׂנְאַ֗י אַצְמִיתֵֽם׃

R.41: You made my enemies run away from me. I destroyed the people who hated me.

alternatives: you gave me their necks to tread on
decisions.reason: To give someone the neck of an enemy is to make the enemy turn and run, showing the back of the neck (Exodus 23:27). It may also picture the victor's foot on the neck of the defeated.

records.source: יְשַׁוְּע֥וּ וְאֵין־מוֹשִׁ֑יעַ עַל־יְ֝הוָ֗ה וְלֹ֣א עָנָֽם׃
records.gloss: They cried for help, but there was no one to save; to YHWH, but not did he answer them.
pieces: They called for help, but no one came to save them; they cried to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them no answer.

L.42: They cried for help, but there was no one to save; [they cried] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not answer them.

R.42: They cried for help, but no one saved them. They even prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them no answer.

decisions.choice: he did not answer them: no help against God's king
decisions.reason: Those who fought the king the LORD had chosen found no help from him, as Saul, when he turned from God, received no answer (1 Samuel 28:6).

decisions.choice: no one to save
decisions.reason: The word for "savior" (moshia') is the one used of God in 17:7.

records.source: וְֽאֶשְׁחָקֵ֗ם כְּעָפָ֥ר עַל־פְּנֵי־ר֑וּחַ כְּטִ֖יט חוּצ֣וֹת אֲרִיקֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And I beat them fine like dust on [the] face of [the] wind; like [the] mud of [the] streets I emptied them out.
pieces: I ground them as fine as dust blown by the wind; I threw them out like mud in the streets.

L.43: And I beat them fine like dust before the wind; like the mud of the streets I poured them out.

R.43: I crushed them into dust that the wind blows away. I threw them out like mud in the street.

decisions.choice: I emptied them out: I threw them away
decisions.reason: The verb (riq) means to empty out or pour away. 2 Samuel 22:43 has a similar word meaning "I stamped them down".

decisions.choice: dust before the wind: something blown away
decisions.reason: As chaff before the wind (1:4; 35:5).

records.source: תְּפַלְּטֵנִי֮ מֵרִ֪יבֵ֫י עָ֥ם תְּ֭שִׂימֵנִי לְרֹ֣אשׁ גּוֹיִ֑ם עַ֖ם לֹא־יָדַ֣עְתִּי יַֽעַבְדֽוּנִי׃
records.gloss: You delivered me from [the] strifes of [the] people; you made me [the] head of nations; a people I did not know serve me.
pieces: You set me free from the people's quarrels; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put me at the head of the nations. A nation I never knew now serves me.

L.44: You delivered me from the strifes of the people; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made me the head of nations; a people I did not know serve me.

R.44: You saved me when people fought against me. You made me ruler over other nations. People I did not even know now serve me.

decisions.choice: the strifes of the people: conflict at home
decisions.reason: "The people" is most likely Israel, and the strife the revolts and divisions within it, from Saul to Absalom (2 Samuel 22:44 reads "my people"). It may instead mean the attacks of other peoples.

decisions.choice: head of nations: ruler over other peoples
decisions.reason: David's kingdom came to include Edom, Moab, Ammon and Aram (2 Samuel 8).

records.source: לְשֵׁ֣מַֽע אֹ֭זֶן יִשָּׁ֣מְעוּ לִ֑י בְּנֵֽי־נֵ֝כָ֗ר יְכַחֲשׁוּ־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: At [the] hearing of [the] ear they obey me; sons of foreignness cringe to me.
pieces: The moment they hear, they obey me; foreigners come to me cringing.

L.45: At the hearing of the ear they obey me; sons of foreign lands cringe before me.

R.45: The moment people from other lands hear about me, they obey me. They bow before me, afraid.

decisions.choice: cringe: give false or forced submission
decisions.reason: The verb (kachash) means to deceive or deny; here it is the forced, insincere humility of the defeated (66:3; Deuteronomy 33:29).

decisions.choice: sons of foreignness: foreigners
decisions.reason: "Sons of" names a group by what it belongs to.

records.source: בְּנֵי־נֵכָ֥ר יִבֹּ֑לוּ וְ֝יַחְרְג֗וּ מִֽמִּסְגְּרֽוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Sons of foreignness wither, and come trembling from their strongholds.
pieces: Foreigners lose heart; they come out of their fortresses shaking.

L.46: Sons of foreign lands wither, and they come trembling out of their strongholds.

R.46: They lose their courage. They come out of their hiding places, shaking with fear.

decisions.choice: come trembling: rare verb
decisions.reason: The verb (charag) is found only here; a related word suggests trembling (compare Micah 7:17). 2 Samuel 22:46 has a different verb, possibly "they limp out" or "they gird themselves".

decisions.choice: wither: lose heart
decisions.reason: Like a plant drying up, their courage fails (Exodus 18:18 uses the same verb).

records.source: חַי־יְ֭הוָה וּבָר֣וּךְ צוּרִ֑י וְ֝יָר֗וּם אֱלוֹהֵ֥י יִשְׁעִֽי׃
records.gloss: Living [is] YHWH, and blessed [be] my rock, and may be exalted [the] God of my salvation,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is alive! Blessed be my rock! May the God who saves me be lifted high,

L.47: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} lives! And blessed [be] my rock, and may the God of my salvation be exalted,

R.47: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is alive! Praise God, who is my rock! Praise the God who saves me!

decisions.choice: The LORD lives: the living God
decisions.reason: The words are used in oaths ("as the LORD lives", 1 Samuel 14:39); here they are a shout of praise. The LORD, unlike idols, is alive and acts (Jeremiah 10:10).

decisions.choice: blessed: praised
decisions.reason: As in 16:7.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The praise continues through verse 49, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: הָאֵ֗ל הַנּוֹתֵ֣ן נְקָמ֣וֹת לִ֑י וַיַּדְבֵּ֖ר עַמִּ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽי׃
records.gloss: the God who gives vengeances for me and has subdued peoples under me,
pieces: the God who avenges me and brings nations under my rule,

L.48: the God who gives vengeance for me and has subdued peoples under me,

R.48: God punishes my enemies for me. He makes nations obey me.

decisions.choice: vengeance: God's just punishment
decisions.reason: Vengeance (neqamah) belongs to God (Deuteronomy 32:35). David does not take it for himself; God gives it, setting right the wrong done to him.

decisions.choice: subdued: brought under control
decisions.reason: The verb (davar) here means to bring under or subdue (47:4 uses it so).

records.source: מְפַלְּטִ֗י מֵאֹ֫יְבָ֥י אַ֣ף מִן־קָ֭מַי תְּרוֹמְמֵ֑נִי מֵאִ֥ישׁ חָ֝מָ֗ס תַּצִּילֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: delivering me from my enemies; indeed, above those who rise against me you exalt me; from a man of violence you rescue me.
pieces: who saves me from my enemies. You raise me high above my attackers; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save me from the violent man.

L.49: who delivers me from my enemies; indeed, above those who rise against me {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} exalt me; from a man of violence {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rescue me.

R.49: He saves me from my enemies. You lift me high above people who attack me. You save me from the violent man.

decisions.choice: a man of violence: perhaps Saul
decisions.reason: The singular may point to one enemy, Saul (verse 1), or stand for every violent enemy (140:2, 5).

decisions.choice: you exalt me: from "he" to "you"
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, the song turns from speaking of God to speaking to him.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֤ן׀אוֹדְךָ֖ בַגּוֹיִ֥ם׀יְהוָ֑ה וּלְשִׁמְךָ֥ אֲזַמֵּֽרָה׃
records.gloss: Therefore I will thank you among the nations, YHWH, and to your name I will sing praises.
pieces: That is why I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks among the nations, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and sing praise to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

L.50: Therefore I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the nations, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name I will sing praises.

R.50: So, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in front of people from every nation. I will sing praises to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: among the nations: quoted in Romans 15:9
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line to show that Scripture foresaw people of every nation praising God through Christ (Romans 15:9).

decisions.choice: your name: God himself as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: As in 5:12 and 9:3.

records.source: מַגְדִּיל֮ יְשׁוּע֪וֹת מַ֫לְכּ֥וֹ וְעֹ֤שֶׂה חֶ֨סֶד׀לִמְשִׁיח֗וֹ לְדָוִ֥ד וּלְזַרְע֗וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: making great [the] salvations of his king, and doing loyal love to his anointed, to David and to his offspring forever.
pieces: Great are the victories {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} grants {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps faith in loyal love with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed one, with David and his line for all time."

L.51: [He is] making great the salvations of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king, and showing loyal love to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed, to David and to his offspring forever."

R.51: He makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king win great battles. He always shows faithful love to the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose, David, and to his children and grandchildren forever."

decisions.choice: making great: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this word slightly differently from the form its notes say to read. The words follow the form to be read, "making great". In 2 Samuel 22:51 the matching word can be read as "tower".

decisions.choice: salvations: victories
decisions.reason: The plural of yeshu'ah (13:6) here means acts of rescue, victories in battle.

decisions.choice: his anointed, David and his offspring forever: the promise to David
decisions.reason: The king anointed by God (1 Samuel 16:13) is David, and the song ends with God's promise of a lasting line (2 Samuel 7:12-16). "Anointed" (mashiach) is the word behind "Messiah" and "Christ", and the promise was later understood to point to the Messiah.

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: As in 13:6.

decisions.choice: loyal love (B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: As in 13:6.

decisions.choice: the king he chose
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing meant: choosing someone as king.
